name: Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra
role: Parliamentary political alliance (Greens and Left Alliance)
notes: Left-green political alliance formed by Sinistra Italiana and Europa Verde; tabled multiple budget amendments and the 2026 "Restituzione fiscale" wealth tax package.

name: Sinistra Italiana
notes: Constituent party of Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra; co-sponsored the 2020 Orfini-Fratoianni budget amendment and 2024–2026 wealth tax proposals.

name: Europa Verde
notes: Constituent green party of Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra; co-proposed the 2026 "Restituzione fiscale" annual wealth tax over EUR 5.4m.

name: Partito della Rifondazione Comunista
notes: Co-promoted the 2026 popular initiative bill "1% Equo" ("Imposta grandi patrimoni") for a 1% to 3.5% progressive annual wealth tax above EUR 2m.

name: Rifondazione Comunista — Federazione di Lucca
role: Provincial federation of Partito della Rifondazione Comunista
notes: Organised municipal signature collection across Lucca, Capannori, Porcari, Altopascio, Borgo a Mozzano, Coreglia Antelminelli, Barga, Bagni di Lucca and Castelnuovo di Garfagnana for the 1% Equo wealth tax bill.

name: Comitato 1% Equo
role: Promoting committee of the "Imposta grandi patrimoni" popular initiative bill
notes: Campaign committee that filed the popular initiative bill "Imposta grandi patrimoni" at the Court of Cassation on 7 May 2026 and collected over 65,000 signatures.

name: Movimento 5 Stelle
notes: In its September 2026 Nova programmatic points put to a member vote, M5S proposed a national progressive levy on large financial assets (excluding small savings, pensions and government bonds) plus a common EU tax on ultra-large fortunes and an exit tax.

name: CGIL
role: National trade union confederation (Confederazione Generale Italiana del Lavoro)
notes: Italy's largest trade union confederation; proposed a 1.3%–1.5% annual solidarity contribution on net wealth above EUR 2m (richest 1%, ~500,000 taxpayers, est. EUR 26bn/year).

name: Oxfam Italia
role: Anti-poverty and economic justice NGO; coordinator of #LaGrandeRicchezza and Agenda Tax the Rich for Italy
notes: Coordinated the Italian campaign #LaGrandeRicchezza for the European Citizens' Initiative Tax the Rich and presented the May 2024 Manifesto of 134 economists at the Italian Senate.

name: Patriotic Millionaires
role: International network of high-net-worth individuals advocating higher taxes on extreme wealth
notes: Co-organised the 22 May 2024 Italian Senate roundtable with Oxfam Italia presenting the Agenda Tax the Rich for Italy and commissioned the G20/Italian millionaires poll (79% of surveyed Italian millionaires in favour).

name: Campagna Sbilanciamoci!
role: Civil-society coalition of 54 organisations publishing the annual Controfinanziaria alternative budget
notes: Coalition of 54 associations, NGOs and networks founded in 1999; its annual Controfinanziaria proposes an "Imposta sulle grandi ricchezze" (progressive net wealth tax starting at EUR 1m up to 2% above EUR 500m, est. EUR 24bn/year).

name: Forum Disuguaglianze e Diversità
role: Research and advocacy alliance on inequality and social justice
notes: Co-founded and coordinated by Fabrizio Barca; proposed a progressive wealth tax from EUR 1m (up to 2% above EUR 50m) alongside a progressive inheritance tax to fund a EUR 15,000 universal endowment for 18-year-olds.

name: Fondazione Demo
role: Cultural and policy foundation close to the Democratic Party
notes: Policy foundation chaired by Gianni Cuperlo whose economics working group (coordinated by Emanuele Felice and Vincenzo Visco) drafted a 2–3% national Zucman-style wealth tax on fortunes above EUR 100m.

notes: Secretary of the Democratic Party (since 2023); endorsed Lula's G20 proposal for an international/European billionaire wealth tax and stated that taxing large fortunes is "not a taboo", preferring a coordinated European or global level.

name: Maurizio Acerbo
role: National Secretary, Partito della Rifondazione Comunista
notes: National Secretary of Rifondazione Comunista and former MP from Pescara; first signatory of the 7 May 2026 1% Equo popular initiative wealth tax bill.

name: Anna Bruna Camposampiero
role: National Directorate Member, Partito della Rifondazione Comunista
notes: Member of the National Directorate of Rifondazione Comunista (Cinisello Balsamo, Milan); first signatory of the 7 May 2026 1% Equo wealth tax bill.

name: Elena Coccia
role: Lawyer; Former Municipal and Metropolitan Councillor of Naples
notes: Labour lawyer and former municipal and metropolitan councillor in Naples; first signatory of the 7 May 2026 1% Equo wealth tax bill.

name: Francesca Fornario
notes: Journalist and satirical author; first signatory of the 7 May 2026 1% Equo popular initiative wealth tax bill.

name: Alfonso Gianni
role: Former Undersecretary of Economic Development; President of CESTES
notes: Former MP and Undersecretary of Economic Development (2006–2008); first signatory of the 7 May 2026 1% Equo wealth tax bill.

name: Matteo Prencipe
notes: National Coordinator of Comitato 1% Equo; first signatory of the 7 May 2026 popular initiative wealth tax bill.

name: Rosa Rinaldi
role: Former Undersecretary of Labour; Former Vice-President of the Party of the European Left
notes: Former FIOM-CGIL trade unionist and Undersecretary of Labour (2006–2008); first signatory of the 7 May 2026 1% Equo wealth tax bill.

name: Nadia Rosa
notes: Former Mayor of Lonate Pozzolo (Varese); first signatory of the 7 May 2026 1% Equo popular initiative wealth tax bill.

name: Benedetta Sabene
role: Writer and editorial staff member, Servizio Pubblico
notes: Journalist and essayist; first signatory of the 7 May 2026 1% Equo popular initiative wealth tax bill.

name: Giuseppe Civati
role: Founder of Possibile; Publisher (People); Former Member of the Chamber of Deputies
location: Italy > Lombardy > Monza e della Brianza > Monza
notes: Former MP (2013–2018) and founder of Possibile; published a January 2026 op-ed calling for a unified progressive proposal for a wealth tax on large fortunes.

name: Sandro Repetto
role: Member of the Provincial Council of Bolzano and Regional Council of Trentino-Alto Adige; Democratic Party Group Leader
affiliation: Consiglio della Provincia autonoma di Bolzano
notes: PD group leader in the Provincial Council of Bolzano and Regional Councillor of Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol; co-sponsored Voto n. 39/25 (Bolzano) and Voto n. 18 (Trentino-Alto Adige) "Tax the Rich" calling for a wealth tax on large fortunes.

name: Brigitte Foppa
role: Member of the Provincial Council of Bolzano and Regional Council of Trentino-Alto Adige; Verdi-Grüne-Vërc Group Leader
affiliation: Consiglio della Provincia autonoma di Bolzano
notes: Leader of Verdi-Grüne-Vërc in the Provincial Council of Bolzano and Regional Councillor of Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol; co-sponsored Voto n. 39/25 (Bolzano) and Voto n. 18 (Trentino-Alto Adige) "Tax the Rich".

name: Maurizio Landini
notes: General Secretary of CGIL (since 2019); proposed a 1.3%–1.5% annual solidarity contribution on net wealth above EUR 2m (richest 500,000 taxpayers) raising EUR 26bn/year.

name: Mikhail Maslennikov
role: Economic Justice Policy Advisor, Oxfam Italia
notes: Policy advisor on economic and fiscal justice at Oxfam Italia; spokesperson for the #LaGrandeRicchezza campaign and the Agenda Tax the Rich for Italy.

name: Carlo De Benedetti
role: Industrialist and publisher (Publisher of Domani; Former Chairman of Olivetti, CIR and Gruppo Editoriale L'Espresso)
notes: Italian billionaire industrialist and newspaper publisher; has repeatedly called in interviews for a progressive wealth tax (tassa patrimoniale progressiva) to fund a sharp cut in labour taxes.

name: Flavio Insinna
notes: Popular Italian actor and television host; publicly declared in February 2021 that as a privileged earner he would gladly pay a wealth tax and urged its rapid adoption.

name: Chiara Brusini
notes: Economics journalist at Il Fatto Quotidiano; authored analysis pieces defending the 134 economists' progressive wealth tax manifesto as a solid, necessary fiscal reform.

name: Giuliano Laccetti
notes: Commentator at Terra Mia; authored a September 2026 op-ed endorsing the Felice-Visco 2–3% wealth tax above EUR 100m.

name: Andrea Di Turi
notes: Economic journalist; authored a July 2024 column arguing that public funds exist if governments tax the ultra-rich as proposed by Patriotic Millionaires, Oxfam and Gabriel Zucman.
